title: Why Does Water Ice Survive 430°C Heat on Mercury?
altTitle: How Does Mercury Hide Water Ice at 430°C?
description:
Every Planet Explained in 12 Minutes (Mercury to Neptune)

On Mercury, the Sun's closest planet, why does water ice survive 430-degree heat? The ice hides in polar craters that never see sunlight. At 58 million kilometres out, sunlight shines up to seven times brighter than on Earth, yet without an atmosphere to retain heat, night plunges to minus 180 degrees Celsius. In 1965, Italian mathematician Giuseppe Colombo solved its spin mystery.

Watch the full film on @OrbitWithBen: Every Planet Explained in 12 Minutes (Mercury to Neptune)

Sources: NASA Science, Mercury Facts — 58 million km average distance (0.4 AU), up to 7× brighter sunlight, 430 °C daytime highs, −180 °C nighttime lows, and water ice in permanently shadowed polar craters (https://science.nasa.gov/mercury/facts/) · NASA Science, BepiColombo & MESSENGER — Giuseppe Colombo (1920–1984) 3:2 spin-orbit resonance and MESSENGER polar water-ice verification (https://science.nasa.gov/mission/bepicolombo/) · Colombo, G. (1965), Nature 208, 575 (https://doi.org/10.1038/208575a0) · NASA Photojournal PIA19411 — MESSENGER north polar water-ice mosaic.

Image credits: NASA/Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory/Carnegie Institution of Washington (MESSENGER: PIA17386, PIA16853, PIA19411, PIA15162, PIA11364).

Pictures: NASA/Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory/Carnegie Institution of Washington MESSENGER imagery alongside original animated explainers, with AI-assisted voice and editing. Facts: every number is checked against the sources listed above.
